name: Marwari (Pakistan)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the second reader's note)
new_statements.check: reported by the second reader, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Spot-checked four silent sources in the folder: (1) — only the survey-wide note 'When it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used' (LSI intro, p. 10); the Western Marwari / Thali / Dhatki of Thar and Parkar sketch (printed pp. 119-123) has no accent, stress or tone statement; (2) Burns 1987) — 'stress' hits are only 'seamstress', 'mistress', 'stressed the importance'; the single phonology remark is the scoring note 'without much knowledge of the phonology of the language' (p. 5-6); silent; (3) CONTEXT_Jhatial_Khan_2021 PDF (extracted text) — no stress/accent/tone/phonology terms; (4) — dialect list and lexical-similarity figures only, no phonology. Nothing missed.

sources.citation: Bahl, Kali Charan. 1980. Adhunik Rajasthani ka samracanatmak vyakaran / A structural grammar of modern Rajasthani. Jodhpur: Rajasthani Shodh Sansthan (Hindi).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Already held by the project under marw1260 (archive.org DLI 2015.403653); states a contrastive neutral vs rising accent with minimal pairs but no default placement rule; Indian Marwari identity (marw1260). Listed so the catalog can decide whether to carry it over to the Pakistani variety with an identity note.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 registration authority, code page for mve (iso639-3.sil.org/code/mve); Glottolog 5.1/5.3 languoid marw1256 (0 descriptive references, 8 refs total).
sources.note: No documentation beyond Ethnologue/Glottolog/Wikipedia; Glottolog's subclassification note cites Grainger & Grainger 1980 pp. 38-39.

Phonology section (vowels/consonants from Mukherjee 2011 LSI Rajasthan = Indian Marwari) says nothing about stress; Pakistan paragraphs give only Ethnologue lexical-similarity data (Utradi, Jaxorati, Larecha; Uganyo, Bhattipo, Khadali subdialects).

sources.citation: Burns, David S. 1987. Proficiency in and attitudes towards the Sindhi language amongst Marwari and Dhati Bhils in Southern Sindh: which is the best New Testament medium for them? High Wycombe: Pakistan Group (SIL/Wycliffe survey report).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic bilingualism survey; the only phonological remark is a scoring note ('Marwari z becomes j, s becomes xh.. without much knowledge of the phonology of the language', pp. 5-6). Bibliography cites Grainger & Grainger 1980 and Payne 1986 'A background Dhati study' (unpublished).

sources.citation: Bahl, Kali Charan. 1980. A structural grammar of modern Rajasthani. Jodhpur (Indian Marwari, marw1260) -- read and quoted by the marw1260 check; and Bhawnani 1979 Thari/Dhatki (dhat1238 check).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not this language: Bahl 1980 (Jodhpur/Bikaner Marwari) lists a contrastive neutral vs rising accent (svaraghat) with minimal pairs and no default-placement rule; Bhawnani 1979 (Dhatki) lists only nasalisation and junctures as suprasegmentals and is silent on stress. Recorded here for context only, per the sibling files.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1908. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX pt. II: Specimens of the Rajasthani and Gujarati. Calcutta. Western Marwari sketch, Thali of Jaisalmer (pp. 119ff) and 'Mixed Marwari and Sindhi' / Dhatki of Thar and Parkar (pp. 122ff).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent for the Marwari of Sindh/Thali/Dhatki; the only accent remark in the volume is the survey-wide transliteration note 'When it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used.' The Thali sketch notes only Sindhi-type final short -a and short vowels.

sources.citation: Gusain, Lakhan. 2004. Marwari. Languages of the World/Materials 427. Munich: LINCOM Europa.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only modern sketch of Marwari with an explicit suprasegmentals section (author's blurb: 'vowels, consonants, diphthongs, and suprasegmentals.. tones'); describes Indian (Jodhpur) Marwari, so any statement would carry an identity note (marw1260), but it is the nearest published stress statement for the Marwari cluster.
